en: The Noble Dhāraṇī Named *Ārya-śrī-grahamātṛkā*. Om! Homage to the Blessed One, the Noble Mother of the Planets (*Grahamātṛkā*). Om! Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Thus have I heard: at one time, in the great city of Ḍākavatī, [there were] many gods, nāgas, ...
Yakṣas, Gandharvas, Suras, Garuḍas,
Kinnaras, Mahoragas, Apsarases, and others [worship] Āditya, Soma, Maṅgala, Budha, Bṛhaspati, Śukra, and Śanaiścara.

Praised by Rāhu, Ketu, and the twenty-eight lunar mansions and other deities, he dwelt upon a lion throne empowered by the empowerment of the manifestation known as the Array of the Great Vajra Samaya Ornament.
Together with many hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas.
Namely as follows:
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrasena.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrabināyaka.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Vajrabir-kurbi-tena.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bajracāpahasta.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrādhipa.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrālaṃkāra.
Furthermore, O Vajranabha, by a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Jyotirvajra.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Lokaśrī.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmaketu and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnaketu.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva with his mouth opened wide.
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī.
By the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Maitreya.
Surrounded and honored by hundreds of thousands of great bodhisattvas headed by these very ones, the Blessed One was teaching this Dharma discourse.

He proclaimed the holy life (*brahmacarya*) that is virtuous in the beginning, virtuous in the middle, and virtuous in the end; excellent in meaning and excellent in phrasing; solitary, complete, pure, and stainless.

Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having looked upon that circle of the assembly, rose from his seat and, through the empowerment of his supernormal power (*ṛddhyadhiṣṭhāna*), circumambulated the Blessed One hundreds of thousands of times.

Having performed his duties, bowed down, and sat before him, Ratnagarbha ascended the couch with grace, surveyed that circle of the assembly, placed his vajra-palms at his own heart, and addressed the Blessed One as follows:
And the planets, as well as those who are gentle, those of fierce form, those who are wrathful, those of terrible form, and those who are cruel, of cruel form—they do not harm living beings here.
They take away the life-breath of some.
And they cause afflictions for some.
And for some, they act as takers of their vitality.
They seize the property of some, and they shorten the lifespan of long-lived beings;
in this way, they cause all sentient beings to be afflicted by calamities.
"Therefore, may the Blessed One teach this Dharma discourse by which all sentient beings will have protection from all calamities.

The Blessed One said: "Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi! It is well that you, having generated a compassionate thought for the sake, welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings, inquire of the Tathāgata, the perfectly awakened one, regarding this most secret of secrets."
Listen to that well and thoroughly; attend to it, and I shall speak.

The divine offerings, the water for the feet (*argha*), and the recitation (*jāpya*)—the most secret among secrets—for the planets of fierce form with extremely terrifying faces, are all described according to their sequence and the distinctions of their colors; when they are thus worshipped, those planets, who are like the slayers of Yama, are propitiated and pacified.
The Debatas, Apsarases, Kinnaras, and Mahoragas.
Yakṣas and rākṣasas, as well as humans and non-humans.
And even those who are enraged become pacified by the power of his great grace.
I shall now proclaim their worship and also their mantras in due order.

Then indeed, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, having emitted from his own heart a web of light-rays named Karuṇāvikrīḍita, caused it to enter the crowns of the planets.
At that very moment, all the planets, led by Āditya, rose up and said to the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Samyaksaṃbuddha: "May the Blessed One grant such a collection of Dharma-discourses as this;
we shall provide protection for the Dharma-preacher who has become [the possessor of] such a [discourse]."

The protection of what is hidden, the securing of possessions, their preservation, the performance of rites for peace and well-being, the avoidance of punishment, the avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison,
and the destruction of poison.
We shall perform the binding of the boundary and the binding of the earth.
Then indeed, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, spoke the mantra-worship of the planets.
Oṃ megholkāya svāhā.
Oṃ, svāhā to the Cool-rayed One!
Oṃ, svāhā to the youth with red limbs!
To the one who bestows protection, svāhā!
Svāhā to the one who is the abode of enjoyment! Svāhā to the supreme among asuras!
Oṃ, svāhā to the one of black complexion!
Oṃ rāhave svāhā.
Oṃ, svāhā to Jyotiketu!

O Vajrapāṇi, these heart-mantras of the nine planets are effective when recited. One should contemplate them in their proper sequence according to the distinction of their colors within a fragrant mandala. In the center of a lotus, one should visualize a peaked pavilion measuring twelve finger-breadths, square in shape, adorned with four doors, and equipped with a wheel.

In the center of that, upon a white lotus on a mandala of saffron and fragrance, some [visualize] the god Bhāskara, assuming the form of an ascetic, red in color, possessing a splendor equal to ten million thousand suns, the hue of vermilion, his body garlanded with radiance.
To him, milk-rice should be given.
The incense of *kunduru*.
Oṃ Megholkāya svāhā. || 1 ||

In the eastern direction, upon a red lotus and a circular mandala of priyaṅgu fragrance, Soma is to be known as a Brāhmaṇa; he is white in color, wears a crown of matted hair, holds a rosary and a water-pot with his two hands, and is adorned with kumuda flowers.
To this, incense of *śrīvāsa* should be offered.
The food consists of either rice cooked with ghee.
Om, salutations to the moon, the immortal one, the embodiment of valor, the cool-rayed one; svāhā.
In the southern direction, upon a white lotus and a circular mandala of sandalwood fragrance, is Bhikṣumaṅgāra, described as being red in color, wearing a jewel crown, and holding a spear.
One with a scar on the hand,
who eats fish and meat.
Or rice with molasses as food.
Guggulu incense.
Oṃ namo raktāṅgāya saujvala-kumārāya svāhā || 3 ||
In the western direction, upon a red lotus and a circular mandala of black agallochum incense, there is the student Budha; he is yellow in color, with a red beard, and holds a rosary and a water-pot.
The food consists of fish, mung beans, and black gram porridge; the incense, fragrance, and flavor [are likewise].
Oṃ, obeisance and svāhā to the Prince, to Budha, who is of a beautiful golden hue. || 4 ||

In the northern direction, upon a white lotus on a fragrant pedestal of Devadāru wood, is the Guru as a wandering ascetic (parivrājaka), with the luster of molten gold, possessing red beard and mustache, and holding a rosary and a water-pot (kamaṇḍalu).
To him, one should offer curd-rice, boiled rice, milk, or ghee and honey, and incense.
Oṃ, salutation to Bṛhaspati, who is red in color, for the sake of emergence; svāhā to the one who bestows enjoyments! 5.

In the southeastern direction, upon a red lotus and a sandalwood-scented mandala, is [the deity] Śukla-pāśa-paraśu-brahmacārī, the color of cow’s milk, holding a choice lotus, matted hair, a crown, rosary beads, and a water-pot.
To him, a meal of milk should be given.
Camphor incense.
Oṃ, homage to the Lord of the White One, the Supreme among Asuras; svāhā to Bīraha! || 6 ||
In the southwest direction, upon a white lotus and a seat of blue sandalwood paste, is Saturn (Śanaiścara);
he is to be known as black in color, a mendicant (kṣapaṇaka), with a hood, nectar, yellow matted hair, and a beard, holding a rosary and a *khikhirikā* staff.
Food, fish, meat, mung-bean curry, incense, fragrance, and flavor.
Oṃ, to Śaninī, to Lāmbhosa, to the Black One, to the one of black complexion, to the eater of the black, svāhā! || 7 ||

In the northwestern direction, upon a mandala of fragrant *tagara* and *pāṭī* flowers atop a pool of red water, is the King Kāpālika, whose color resembles a *rājāvarta* gem. He has one face and four arms, is terrifying, and his forehead is furrowed with a fierce frown. Amidst clouds of five colors, he stands upon the moon, sun, and lotus with two of his hands, while the other two hold a skull-cup and a staff. His food offering should consist of meat and wine.
One should offer oblations of sesame, kṛsarā, and discolored incense.
Oṃ, homage to the one with a formidable face, seated upon blood, resembling collyrium and a bee, possessing the splendor of nectar; svāhā! || 8 ||
In the northeastern direction, the Raktaśara, Rūha, and Paripṛkkā plants, as well as the Gandhamaṇḍalaka, constitute the banner of Caṇḍāla.
Smoke-colored, with palms joined in reverence, bearing his own tail in the form of a serpent, feeding on iron, holding a vessel of clarified butter, and possessing fragrant resin incense;
*oṃ dhūmrāmma varṇasaṃnibhāya jyotike-tave svāhā* || 9 ||
At the eastern gate of the mandala is the Buddha, the Blessed One; at the southern gate is Vajrapāṇi.
At the western gate is Lokanātha.
At the northern gate is Mañjuśrīkumāra; in the northeast is the venerable Mahādevī, who is youthful, three-faced,
and three-eyed.

She has six arms; with two hands she performs the *vyākhyāna* (teaching) mudrā; the right [hands] hold a vajra and the left hold a lotus and a bow. She wears a jeweled crown, sits upon a blue vajra-paryaṅka, rests on a moon seat, possesses sixteen aspects, and is adorned with all ornaments.
Outside the eastern gate of the mandala is the food offering for Dhṛtarāṣṭra, consisting of curd-rice.
For Virūḍhaka, curd with black gram rice.
In the west, [the offering] for Virūpākṣa is milk-rice.
To the north is the food of Kubera, consisting of curd and beans.
Banners should be offered according to the sequence of their respective colors, together with vermilion.
Likewise, worship should be performed with flowers according to the distinction of their sequential colors.

A lamp should be offered for each [deity], having filled a conch with ghee and honey and having cast five jewels into it; an offering (argha) should be presented, and it should be given at the head of all.
Their complexion, hand postures, seats, mudrās, and emblems are as follows.
Homage to all the Tathāgatas, the fulfillers of all, to those whose devotion is completely fulfilled, svāhā!
One should recite the mantra of the Three Jewels.
The seven, seven, and eight mantras, each one by one.
Thus worshipped, all the planetary deities of various forms [are propitiated].
It bestows vast enjoyments and also generates good fortune.
O Vajrapāṇi, these heart-mantras of the nine planets are effective when recited.

Having prepared a fragrant mandala according to the sequence and classification of colors, one should worship [the deities] in the center of the mandala, which measures twelve finger-breadths, using a vessel made of copper, clay, silver, or other materials, and having offered the *argha* water;

then, after reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, one should subsequently recite the mantra-words of the *dhāraṇī* named *Grahamātṛkā*, the Mother of the Planets, seven times, O Vajrapāṇi.
Then all those planets, beginning with the Sun, will provide protection, defense, and guardianship.
All the planets will liberate one from poverty.
One whose life has ended becomes long-lived.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, whatever monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen there may be who are of such a nature as this,
into whose ears it shall fall—
They will not bring about untimely death or die at an improper time.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, whoever shall worship [this] within the circle of planets and recite it day after day, [shall obtain these benefits].
Then all the grahas will completely fulfill every single hope of that Dharma-reciter.
They will also destroy poverty within that family.
Then indeed the Blessed One, Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata,
spoke once more the dhāraṇī named Grahāmātṛkā.
Homage to the Three Jewels.
Homage to the Holder of the Umbrella-Vajra.
Salutation to the one who holds a lotus in her hand.
Oṃ, homage to Kumāra.
Oṃ namaḥ to all the planets, who fulfill all parts; oṃ namaḥ to the lunar mansions.
Oṃ, homage to the twelve zodiac signs!
Oṃ namaḥ. To [the one who is] the [remover] of all calamities.
Namely as follows:

Oṃ buddhe 2 vajre 2 padme 2 sara 2 prasara 2 smara 2 krīḍa 2 krīḍaya 2 mara 2 māraya 2 mardaya 2 ghātaya 2! Cut through 2, split apart 2 all obstacles for me and for all sentient beings! Destroy 2 all obstacles! Accomplish 2! Fulfill the purpose of myself and my retinue, as well as that of all sentient beings! Cast away 2 all misdeeds from myself and my retinue! Be peaceful 2! Be tamed 2!

2 Dāpaya 2! O Blessed One, show yourself! Protect me and all sentient beings! Ward off the afflictions caused by all seizing spirits (*graha*) and constellations (*nakṣatra*)! O Blessed One, bring about prosperity! Accomplish the Great Illusion (*mahāmāyā*)! Destroy all the wicked! 2 Nāśaya 2! All my sins and those of my retinue—Candre 2! Candrani 2! Turu 2! Muru 2! Mū 2! Mūñca 2! In existence after existence, O Fierce One, O Fierce One, O You who heat with fierce heat, fulfill [our needs], O Blessed One!
May all beings fulfill their heart's desires; ward off all afflictions caused by the stars and planets. Through the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas, may this be so at this empowered moment. Svāhā!
Oṃ bāhā hūṃ svāhā.
Hrīṃ bāhā.
The yoke-pole, svāhā!
Dhīḥ svāhā!
Om, svāhā to Āditya!
Oṃ, svāhā to Soma!
Oṃ, svāhā to Dharaṇīputra; oṃ, svāhā to Ambuda; oṃ, svāhā to Bṛhaspati; oṃ, svāhā to Śukra.
Oṃ, svāhā to the one who issues forth thunderbolts!
Oṃ rāhuveśabāha ||
Oṃ ketabesbāhā oṃ buddhāyasbāhā.
Oṃ vajrapāṇaye svāhā.
Her two arms hold a lotus.
Oṃ kumārāya svāhā!
Svāhā to all the planets! Svāhā to all the lunar mansions!

*Oṃ sarvopadravaḥ sarvavidyā huṃ phaṭ svāhā.* O Vajrapāṇi, these dhāraṇīs called the *Grahamātṛkā* should be recited seven times every day during the fortnight of the waxing moon in the month of Kārttika, beginning from the seventh day until the fourteenth— the day of the mandala of planets and constellations— by one who has observed the *poṣadha* vows.
Then, having performed worship for a full day and night on the full moon day, one should have it recited; for him, there shall be no fear of death for ninety-nine years.
There shall be no fear from falling meteors, planetary afflictions, or calamities.
In every birth he takes, he will remember his past lives.
Then all those planets, having replied, "Very well, Blessed One," vanished from sight.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, and the monks were delighted, as were the entire assembly, including the gods, humans, asuras,
garuḍas, and kinnaras.
The mahoragas rejoiced in what was spoken by the Blessed One.
The Dhāraṇī named Āryagrahamātṛkā is completed.
